tool.name: MS DHCP Extended Management
tool.description: Manage Microsoft DHCP servers (IPv4 and IPv6): scopes, options, reservations, failover and a full configuration check.
tool.long_description: Connects to a Microsoft DHCP server (IPv4 and DHCPv6) with the current account, stored credentials or a different login and keeps the failover partners in view. Every scope opens in its own tab with general settings, address pool, options, reservations, exclusions, leases and failover state; findings (errors, warnings, best practice) are calculated while you type and mark the affected fields. New scopes are created from a draft or duplicated from an existing scope, with addresses converted to the new network. Changes on failover scopes can be replicated to the partner automatically (works even when the partner is only reachable via RPC, like the DHCP console). Further pages: server options of every failover server with sync state, failover relationships (expandable to both servers) with all scopes of each server, option definitions (expert mode, locked by default) and a server-wide scan with distribution of findings that also compares everything with the failover partners (scopes, pools, exclusions, options, reservations, relationship settings, classes and definitions). DHCPv6 with the same scope: prefixes, lifetimes, options, reservations by DUID and IAID, exclusions, leases, check, transactions and conflict detection; an IPv4/IPv6 switch selects the view. Optionally the check compares reservations and leases with DNS (name, address, PTR). Detects read-only access (DHCP Users) and hides editing functions accordingly. Talks to the server directly via the Windows DHCP API (RPC) – no PowerShell or WinRM. Replication to the partner uses netsh dhcp from the RSAT DHCP tools (added automatically during installation).

help.text:
MS DHCP Extended Management – quick help

OVERVIEW
  All scopes with ranges, usage and failover. Double-click opens a scope in its own tab.
  "New scope …" opens a draft, "Duplicate …" copies a scope into a new network.

SCOPE TAB
  General: name, lease duration, state and the address pool (start to end, exclusions on their own page).
  Options, reservations, exclusions, leases: changes take effect on the server immediately.
  Findings: errors, warnings, best practice and infos. Double-click applies the suggested fix or jumps to the object.
  A "?" next to a field shows the findings for that field.

IPV6 (DHCPv6)
  The IPv4 | IPv6 switch at the top selects what overview, server options and definitions show. The check and the event log cover both.
  DHCPv6 scopes are always /64. Instead of a lease duration there is a preferred and a valid lifetime, instead of a MAC address DUID and IAID.
  There is no address pool: the whole prefix is handed out, exclusions take addresses out. Windows has no failover for DHCPv6.

FAILOVER
  With auto replication on, a failover scope is transferred to the partner after every change.
  The partner is reached directly via the DHCP interface, falling back to netsh – like the DHCP console.
  Server options are not replicated with the scopes; when editing, the "Copy to partner" tick copies them as well.
  Failover page: one row per relationship, expandable to its two servers; below, all scopes of the selected server.

RIGHTS
  With an account from "DHCP Users" (read only) all editing functions are hidden.
  The "Definitions" page only appears in expert mode (settings) and has to be unlocked there as well.

CLIPBOARD
  Options, reservations and exclusions can be copied between scopes; addresses are converted on request.

KEYS
  Ctrl+W closes the current tab, Del removes, F2 edits, Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V copy and paste.

srvopt.servers_hint:
The connected server and its failover partners. Click a server to see its server options.

"Sync" compares with the counterpart: for the connected server with all partners, for a partner with the connected server. Options set only on the counterpart appear greyed out with "Missing here" – "Edit" takes them over. Options 051 (lease duration) and 081 (DNS settings) are not compared.
fo.concept:
A failover relationship always consists of exactly two servers. A server can have several relationships, though – with the same or with different partners (e.g. load balance for the offices and hot standby for a branch). Every scope belongs to at most one relationship.

The top list shows every relationship as one row. Expanded (arrow, double-click or right arrow key) it shows its two servers below, each with the values from its own view (role, share, state). If the two views do not match, relationship and server are marked red (details in the tooltip).

The bottom list shows all scopes of the selected server – including those in no or in another relationship – and whether they exist on the counterpart.

settings.auto_refresh.description: Checks at the chosen interval whether the server was changed (also via the DHCP console) and reloads the views. Who changed it is shown from the server's event log.

evt.detail_hint: Select an event to see details and notes.
evt.err_title: The event log of {server} cannot be read.
evt.err_access: The signed-in account lacks read permission. On {server} it must be a member of “Event Log Readers” or an administrator.
evt.err_rpc: {server} cannot be reached for the event log. Usually the Windows Firewall blocks the rule group “Remote Event Log Management”.
evt.err_channel: On {server} the DHCP “Operational” event log does not exist or is disabled.
evt.err_link: Open the setup guide in the wiki
evt.hint.scope: Note: a scope was changed (name, pool, state, lease duration …). For failover scopes check replication / the comparison with the partner afterwards.
evt.hint.option: Note: an option value was changed (scope or server option). Clients pick it up at their next lease renewal. For failover scopes the partner needs the same value.
evt.hint.optiondef: Note: an option definition was changed. Deleting a definition also removes all values of that option. Definitions are not copied to the partner automatically.
evt.hint.reservation: Note: a reservation was created, changed or removed. For failover scopes it must exist on the partner too, otherwise the partner may lease the address differently.
evt.hint.exclusion: Note: an exclusion range was changed. The server no longer leases addresses in it; existing leases stay until they expire.
evt.hint.failover: Note: a failover relationship was changed (scopes, mode, MCLT, load balance …). Both servers need the same settings – run the check with “Compare with partners”.
evt.hint.policy: Note: a DHCP policy was changed. Policies are not edited in this tool; see the DHCP console for details.
evt.hint.filter: Note: a MAC filter (allow/deny) was changed. It decides which clients get an address at all.
evt.hint.class: Note: a user or vendor class was changed. Options using this class need it on the partner as well.
evt.hint.server: Note: a server setting was changed (e.g. audit log, database, bindings, conflict detection).
evt.hint.other: Note: the event could not be assigned to an area – see the text and event data.
chk.dns_no_name: The name "{name}" for {ip} cannot be resolved in DNS.
chk.dns_other_ip: The DNS name "{name}" does not point to {ip} but to {detail}.
chk.dns_no_ptr: There is no PTR record (reverse lookup) for {ip} ("{name}").
chk.dns_other_ptr: The PTR record of {ip} points to "{detail}" instead of "{name}".
chk.dns_timeout: DNS check: {n} lookups did not return in time and were skipped.
chk.o6_link_local: {label}: {value} is a link-local address. Clients in other networks cannot reach it.
chk.o6_no_dns: Neither the scope nor the server sets DNS servers (option 23). DHCPv6 clients then get no DNS servers.
chk.res6_anycast: {obj} is the subnet-router anycast address (interface ID 0) and must not be assigned.
chk.res6_dup_duid: The client DUID {duid} / IAID {iaid} has several reservations: {ips}
chk.res6_excluded: {obj} is inside an exclusion range. That is allowed, reservations still apply.
chk.s6_pref_valid: The preferred lifetime ({pref}) must be shorter than the valid lifetime ({valid}).
chk.srv6_duid_multi: The client DUID {duid} / IAID {iaid} is reserved in several scopes: {list}
chk.srv6_no_binding: The DHCPv6 service is not bound to any network adapter. There are DHCPv6 scopes, but no client gets an answer.
chk.srv6_stateless_purge: Stateless DHCPv6 clients are stored but never purged (purge interval 0).
chk.with_dns_tip: Checks for reservations and active leases whether the name points to the address in DNS and the PTR record matches. Uses this computer's DNS resolver.
chk.x6_reversed: In the exclusion {range} the end lies before the start.
clip.wrong_family: The clipboard data belongs to the other address family (IPv4/IPv6) and cannot be pasted here.
excl6.note: DHCPv6 hands out the whole /64 prefix. Exclusions take addresses out of it and take effect on the server immediately.
lease6.no_duid: No valid DUID is known for {ip}.
log.res6_name_failed: Reservation {ip}: name and description could not be set (the server has no client record yet). Save again once the client has contacted the server.
main.family_tip: Address family for overview, server options and definitions. The check and the event log always cover both.
opt.err_id6: Please enter an option code between 1 and 65535.
res6.err_anycast: Interface ID 0 is the subnet-router anycast address and cannot be reserved.
res6.err_duid: Please enter a valid DUID (2 to 130 bytes hexadecimal, e.g. 00-01-00-01-2c-4f-11-22-00-15-5d-01-02-03).
res6.err_iaid: Please enter an IAID between 0 and 4294967295 (decimal or 0x…).
res6.err_ip: Please enter a valid IPv6 address.
res6.hint: DHCPv6 identifies a client by DUID and IAID, not by MAC address. Both are shown in the lease ("Leases" page, "To reservation") or on Windows in "ipconfig /all" (DHCPv6 Client DUID, DHCPv6 IAID).
scan.dns: DNS check of reservations and leases …
scope6.err_lifetime: Please enter the lifetimes as days.hh:mm:ss, e.g. 8.00:00:00.
scope6.err_plen: Windows only supports /64 prefixes for DHCPv6 scopes.
scope6.err_pref_valid: The preferred lifetime must be shorter than the valid lifetime.
scope6.err_prefix: Please enter a valid IPv6 prefix, e.g. 2001:db8:10::/64.
scope6.hint: Prefix is always /64. New scopes are created inactive first, options and exclusions are copied, and only then activated (if selected). If a step fails, everything is rolled back.
scope6.lifetime_hint: Preferred lifetime: how long the client uses the address for new connections. Valid lifetime: after that it loses the address. The preferred lifetime has to be shorter. Windows sets T1 and T2 to 50 % and 80 % of the preferred lifetime.
scope6.no_pool_hint: DHCPv6 hands out addresses from the whole /64 prefix. Addresses that must not be assigned belong on the "Exclusions" page. Windows has no failover for DHCPv6.
scope6.preference_tip: Server preference 0–255 in replies. With several DHCPv6 servers the client picks the one with the highest value.
scope6.rapid_tip: Address assignment with two instead of four messages. Only turn on when exactly one DHCPv6 server serves the network.
scope6.unicast_tip: Clients may contact the server directly (unicast) instead of via multicast.

fav.combo_tip: Saved servers with login method and connection settings. Selecting one fills in the login form.

fav.overwrite_q: Overwrite favourite “{name}” with server, login method and connection settings from the login form?
fav.manage_hint: Double-click edits a favourite. The order is the order of the list on the login page. Login method and connection settings are changed in the login form and applied via “Save as favourite” › “Overwrite”.
fav.delete_q: Delete favourite “{name}”? Credentials stored in the password manager are kept.
fav.name: Name
fav.hint: A favourite stores the server, login method, user or the reference to stored credentials and the connection settings of the login page. Passwords are never stored in a favourite.
fav.cred_missing: The stored credentials of this favourite no longer exist. Please select credentials and overwrite the favourite.
